curr_de1dcd0ffd.full_pdf_text:
The Inspiring Life of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was born on 15 October 1931 in Rameswaram, a small
town in Tamil Nadu, India. He grew up in a humble family and learned the values
of hard work, honesty, and kindness from his parents. As a child, he helped his
family by distributing newspapers while continuing his studies with great
determination. His love for learning and science led him to become an aerospace
scientist, and he played an important role in India’s space and missile
development programmes. Because of his contributions, he became widely
known as the “Missile Man of India.” In 2002, he became the 11th President of
India, serving the country with humility and inspiring millions of young people to
dream big, work hard, and use their knowledge to help others. Even after his
presidency, he continued to teach and encourage students. Dr. Kalam passed
away on 27 July 2015 while delivering a lecture to students, doing what he loved
most. His life reminds us that great achievements can begin with simple dreams,
sincere effort, and a strong desire to serve our nation.
